Setting up Nova

A few quick questions. You can change most answers later in Settings.

Hi, I’m Nova. A few quick questions to set things up; you can change most answers later in Settings, and "skip" keeps my default. The first three are about this computer: its roles you change later in Settings › Devices, and Settings › Services shows how it runs services.

This is a Linux computer (x64): 5 threads, 18 GB of memory, no GPU Nova can use, 57 GB free on disk. I’d make it the hub of a new Nova network: your phone and other computers join it later. Or, if you already have a Nova hub, this computer can join that instead. (New, or join?)
New network, this computer as hub
This computer is your hub, then. Other devices join it from Settings › Devices.

What is this computer for, besides being the hub? I recommend general server. The others: compute (runs models and other heavy work); storage (keeps models and data); capture source (may run capture; Capture itself stays off until you turn it on). (“Yes” for what I recommend, or say which.)
General server
This hub is for: general server. You can change that in Settings › Devices.

How Nova runs its services here. Recommended: ordinary programs, under Nova’s supervisor. It’s lighter and needs nothing extra. This is how Nova runs its services here. K3s, for container services, isn’t available in this version yet. You can see this in Settings › Services. Switching to K3s will be there once it is available, and it will ask for your explicit confirmation. (“Yes” to go on.)
Ordinary programs, under Nova’s supervisor

K3s, a small Kubernetes Not available yet in this version.

Answer Nova
